page: Amazon Web Services r6id.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor featuring four physical cores and eight vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading. It provides 64 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. In addition to standard networking interfaces supporting a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps, this instance includes 474 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results place the r6id.2xlarge firmly in the middle 50% performance bracket across standard integer, cryptographic, and memory-bound metrics. The instance registered a Geekbench single-core score of 1627.0 and a multi-core score of 6073.0, paired with an uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 59.48 GB/s. For caching workloads, Redis SET operations reached 7.76 million operations per second. However, compute-heavy tasks that exceed thread capacity or lack hardware acceleration show limitations, as evidenced by multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and 7B-parameter LLM inference falling into the lower performance quartiles.

The inclusion of 474 GB of high-speed local NVMe storage combined with a substantial 64 GB memory footprint offers high qualitative cost efficiency for input-output-sensitive operations. Organizations avoid the latency and continuous transfer fees associated with external block storage for temporary files and caches. Due to this balanced allocation of fast local disks and high memory density, the r6id.2xlarge is well-suited for in-memory databases, key-value stores, distributed cache clusters, and medium-scale transactional data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r6id.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The configuration provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 64 GB of DDR4 memory, and a dedicated 474 GB local NVMe SSD instance storage volume. Network throughput is rated at a 3 Gbps baseline. Operating with an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the instance displays solid, consistent benchmark outcomes in the middle 50% tier for general compute and memory bandwidth, reaching 7.76 million Redis SET operations per second. While parallel compute-heavy compression and large language model inference show clear CPU limits, the bundled NVMe disk provides strong qualitative efficiency by eliminating external disk access latencies. This makes the instance suitable for in-memory caching, transactional databases, and fast scratch-space data pipelines.
